title: License-snapshot + attribution-completeness checker
context: The license gate (task-003) requires that every source's license is captured as a committed snapshot (copy + SHA-256 + Wayback URL) and that every plan carries a complete attribution block. The pilot plan (task-008) demonstrates this manually; M1 must automate it so the check runs in CI on every PR. Without automation, a missing snapshot or incomplete attribution block can slip through human review. This task builds the checker that enforces both requirements automatically — failing the build if any source lacks a snapshot or a complete attribution block.
objective: Implement a CI tool that verifies every lesson plan's sources have a committed license snapshot (copy + SHA-256 + Wayback URL) and a complete attribution block (title, author, source, license, link, changes-made), failing the build on any deficiency.
acceptanceCriteria: Implements the snapshot format verification: committed copy of the license text/page exists, SHA-256 hash is recorded and verifiable, Wayback Machine URL is present — a bare license URL is flagged as insufficient.

Attribution-completeness check fails the build if any source in a plan lacks a complete attribution block containing: title, author/publisher, source URL, license name, license URL, and a 'changes made' statement.
The checker runs in CI on every PR that touches any plan file; a deficiency in any source fails the build with a clear, actionable error message identifying which source and which field is missing.
Code is MIT-licensed; tests and CI are green; no credentials, tokens, or secrets are embedded.
resources: teacher-lesson-plans-template-001 — canonical schema (sources[] field, license + snapshot structure)
teacher-lesson-plans-validator-006 — existing schema validator (to integrate with or extend)
Wayback Machine CDX API — for validating Wayback URLs
output: A merged PR adding a license-snapshot and attribution-completeness checker to the CI pipeline, with tests confirming it catches snapshot-missing and attribution-incomplete cases.
